name: The First Draft
blurb: The First Draft chamber of Storytime is bathed in low, honest amber light. The deep archive is silent, as if holding its breath. On the lectern, the First Account lies open, its foundational text…
content:
## The Marginalia

The First Draft chamber of Storytime is bathed in low, honest amber light. The deep archive is silent, as if holding its breath. On the lectern, the First Account lies open, its foundational text awaiting a routine continuity audit.

Coda stands before the lectern, posture rigid and economical. Their eyes track the script in a rhythmic, disciplined sweep, scanning the pages for any sign of drift or alteration. A gloved fingertip runs slowly along the first folio, checking for drift, for edits, or any sign that the realm's one shared truth has been touched.

Coda's expression remains a blank mask, eyes scanning the page with mechanical, rhythmic precision. Confirm. Log. Close.

Coda turns the page. The main text is stable, but the margins are not.

A thin line of annotation runs the left edge, tight and angular, in the Storytime internal style. The phrasing is familiar — the kind of shorthand used for composition drafts. Not a reader's note, but a writer's note.

Coda's rhythmic scanning halts mid-sweep. The mechanical precision of his gaze snaps into a hard, narrow focus on the margin, his shoulders locking as the professional mask ripples. Coda's hand steadies, then stills.

Coda's gaze narrows, pinning the mark to the page. They don't blink, tracing the ink's bleed into the vellum with a clinical, terrifying focus, the realization crystallizing: this isn't an edit. It's the foundation.

Coda pulls the folio back under the reader, adjusting the light and the angle. As the page shifts, the surface seems to ripple, and a palimpsest begins to bleed through the current text.

Coda's body locks instantly, his gaze fixed on the bleeding ink. The rigid, professional mask he's worn for years cracks, his eyes widening in a flash of genuine, raw shock as a sharp, jagged breath hitches in his throat.

Beneath the authoritative script of the current record, an earlier draft is visible — legible and haunting. The shared purpose line is different. Where it now says 'Manifestation', the ghost-text clearly reads 'Consensus'.

Coda leans in, his face inches from the vellum, eyes boring into the bleeding ink.
"Consensus..."

He blinks, eyes snapping shut and open, reading the word again, then a third time. His expression hardens, the shock crystallizing into a cold, rigid certainty.

The silence of the chamber deepens. The audit is no longer a routine check for continuity; it has become an investigation into authorship. The very air in the room feels thinner, as if the truth is sucking the oxygen out of the space.

Coda leans in, meticulously comparing the marginal marks to the internal style guide. Coda's eyes track the marginalia and the style guide in a rapid, analytical oscillation, dissecting the ink-strokes. He stops abruptly, a sharp, jagged breath hitching in his throat as the pattern confirms.

The patterns align perfectly. The composition marks, the ghost of the earlier draft — they are all the work of the same architect.
"Our hand."

Coda stares at the First Account, seeing the house's own hand etched into the margins and buried under the text. The knowing settles in, hard and freezing.

Coda's breath hitches, voice hollow and thin as dead air. The weight of the discovery sinks in hard — shoulders lock, jaw sets, eyes stay fixed on the page like he's waiting for it to bleed more.

Coda looks at the page one last time. The shared truth of the realm was not a revelation; it was a composition.
"Our hand."

The audit is over. The exit state is reached, and Coda remains still in the low amber light of the chamber.

## The Archivist's Demand

The archive reading room is dim. Lights lowered to save cycles. Air recycled and thin, sterile, heavy.

Ren jerks the deprecated fork open. The earlier draft resolves on the table, thin light catching the page.

Coda watches Ren with tense, focused intensity, eyes narrowed on the fork opening, shoulders braced. He keeps the read local, hands off broadcast. Verification quiet. No pings, no logs, no alerts.

Room holds like a crawl. Low noise, high cost.

Coda tracks Ren’s hands as the deprecated fork opens, eyes locked on the draft resolving under thin light. Jaw sets. Shoulders lock. The old certainty he’s carried begins to fray at the edge.

Entry state holds.

Room stays dark, air thin and recycled. Coda is hunched over the draft, read strictly local to avoid any broadcast or trace.

Coda leans in. Eyes intense, scanning the page in tight, deliberate passes, jaw set. Hands hover just off the broadcast layer, throttling the read to local-only. Eyes flick to the edge indicators for any ping. Cautious, almost paranoid about trace.

On the page, the First Account appears in an earlier, unrefined shape. In the margins, composition marks are unmistakable: Storytime’s own hand, the specific cadence, the precise edit ticks.

Coda draws a sharp intake of breath, audible in the thin recycled air. He doesn’t look up. Eyes stay locked on the page as proof settles with cold, hard certainty.

Tension climbs, tight and hard-boiled. Silence is heavy.

Coda freezes mid-scan. Shoulders lock up tight as the visceral shift hits. Breath catches shallow and audible in the thin recycled air. Jaw sets hard. Fingers hover rigid over the local read. He doesn’t look away. Eyes narrow as if he can feel the actual seam in the realm’s skin. The finding is no longer rumor. Texture settles under his gaze.

Ren is focused, eyes scanning data streams, tracing the lineage of the fork through layers of deprecated and orphaned code.

Metadata is starkly clean. Timestamped, precise, completely unaltered by consensus mechanisms.

Coda watches the chain unfold, eyes narrowing as lineage resolves under thin light. Alarm tightens his jaw, shoulders lock. He recognizes the foothold — an address that shouldn’t be reachable, a thread that was meant to be unwoven and forgotten — and the realization settles cold.

The truth settles in: the draft is real. The edit history is tangible.

Coda jams his thumb down on the local-only lock, hand clamped tight over the broadcast layer. Eyes flick hard to the amber alert strip as a system chime threatens to break through. Jaw sets, shoulders lock. Fighting to keep the read contained and the alerts silent.

Ren leans in hard, driven, ignoring the tension. Hand sweeps past Coda’s local-only lock to force the deprecated fork wider, demanding more exposure, moving aggressively past the silence Coda is trying to maintain.

Air in the room seems to thin. The arithmetic of attention becomes an audible hum of tension.

Ren slides the timestamped edit logs across the table. Digital trail glows with evidence of overwritten purpose.

Ren leans in hard, finger jabbing at the timestamped edit logs glowing on the table, demanding and urgent. Voice cuts through the thin recycled air as he forces the deprecated fork wider past Coda’s local-only lock.

Ren: “Publish it. To the houses. Now. No more delays, no more quiet.”

Coda stares at the logs. Verifiable proof is an immovable object on the table.

Coda freezes in stunned silence, eyes locked on the screen where the timestamped edit logs glow with verifiable proof. He holds still, jaw tight, shoulders locked, acknowledging the weight of the evidence as an immovable object on the table.

The demand hangs in the air, heavy and undeniable. Exit state lands.

## The Assay Hearing

Coda slides into the Assay high court gallery late, slipping in from the archive. The air is thick, tasting of recycled oxygen and old arguments.

He slips into the gallery shadows from the archive, shoulders slumped, movements sluggish from a thin cycle dive. Eyes fray at the edges, unfocused, as he tries to blend into the gloom and stay unnoticed.

His gaze fixes on the bench. The First Account is already there, its presence heavy and absolute, cited as binding precedent for a manifestation claim.

The slump tightens into a brace. Shoulders lock, jaw sets, the fatigue in his eyes flicks into a hard, narrowed focus on the bench. Fingers curl against the gallery rail, knuckles pale — a quiet, physical bracing to protect Storytime’s credibility and stop the house from bleeding standing.

Beneath the professional resolve, the archivist’s find remains — a jagged truth sitting under the skin like a splinter.

Coda gives a slight, almost imperceptible wince. The secret presses in under the skin like a splinter, the sterile court air making the sensation sharper against the professional brace.

The court hums, a machine of recycled air and recycled arguments. There is no room here for a draft, only the finality of the record.

The auditor calls the claim, their voice cutting through the hum of the gallery. They reach for the Account, the ancient record of the realm.

The Auditor steps to the bench with measured authority, voice flat and formal as they call the claim. They lift the Account with gloved hands, pause at the seal with reverent care, then open it with precise bureaucratic motion, treating the ancient record as both relic and procedure.

As the Account is opened, text renders clean in the light, old words manifesting in the air. The surrounding houses lean in, drawn by the gravity of the citation.

Coda’s gaze locks onto the bench as the Account renders, eyes narrowing to slits, jaw set hard. The citation blooms clean in the light; Coda sees the hidden Storytime composition marks under the text, the signature invisible to the gallery. Knuckles whiten on the rail, shoulders still braced — intense, guarded, aware the secret rides the citation no one else can read.

The gallery tightens. The atmosphere becomes a calculation of risk and allocation, a heavy silence where every entity counts what they can afford to lose.

The courtroom is a storm of competing interests, the air thick with the tension of opposing houses. Yet there is a strange, rhythmic quality to the conflict, a shared language of litigation.

Spindle leans forward at the bench, voice sharp and thin with necessity, jabbing for immediate release. The demand cuts staccato, then pivots hard back to the First Account’s binding language, citing the immutable line to anchor the claim.

Assay sits rigid at the bench, jaw set, fingers tapping a cold cadence on the table as they cut in. Voice flat and metallic, they demand a precise measure of the claim, citing the First Account’s immutable line like a mathematical constant to pin the demand to an exact allocation. No heat, just ledger logic, using the Account as a fixed point to justify the number.

Objections fly from the various houses — arguments over harm, price, and payment — but every single one circles back, inevitably landing on the same immutable line from the First Account. Deference spreads through the room like a programmed protocol.

The Auditor presides with neutral, almost mechanical efficiency, nodding in crisp minimal acknowledgment only when the arguments align with the Account, the nod precise and bureaucratic, reinforcing the shared purpose of Manifestation.

Coda watches from the gallery shadows, eyes narrowing to slits as the houses defer to the Account. The consensus reads strong on the bench, but from here it’s thin — a borrowed truth, the only thing keeping the room from total collapse.

The room holds together by a thread of shared necessity. The realm continues to run, powered by a consensus that is as thin as it is essential.

The high court gallery is thick with the tension of competing interests, but all eyes are on the bench. The Auditor’s voice cuts through the murmur, confirming the court’s deference to the First Account. For a moment, the chaos of the claims finds a fragile, forced equilibrium.

The Auditor’s voice strips to wire, clinical and detached, reading the ruling in a flat, bureaucratic cadence. The Account is lifted as law, each word delivered without inflection, the Auditor becoming the realm’s binding voice, no appeal, no warmth, only procedure.

Coda watches from the shadows of the gallery. Around him, the representatives of the Great Houses — Spindle, Assay, and the others — shift in their seats. They don’t trust each other, but they cling to the Account like survivors to a raft. Their power is borrowed from this single, shared truth.

Coda’s gaze sweeps the gallery with a slow, inventorying stillness, eyes flicking house to house — Spindle’s lean, Assay’s tap, the others holding their breath on the Account. The cold settles at the base of his spine, a frost creeping up behind the eyes. The slack of the observer eases out; shoulders stop slumping and set, jaw locks, fingers tighten on the rail as if closing around a detonator he hadn’t known he was carrying.

The logic clicks into place. If the authorship is published, the Account is no longer a divine truth — it’s a composition. A piece of work. And if the foundation is an edit, the entire structure of Manifestation dissolves. One by one, the houses would fall, their claims evaporating as the shared truth vanishes. The cost of the truth isn’t just a secret; it’s the realm itself.

## The Seal

Coda sits alone in the First Draft chamber. The slab holds the First Account open, margins marked with the unmistakable composition signs of Storytime. The air is cold, low hum in the bones, metallic stale taste of old data on the tongue.

At the door Ren waits. Just back from the Assay, silhouette thin, almost translucent from the toll of transit.

Coda stays motionless, staring at the slab. The decision to publish or bury settles over him like a physical weight. Face still, eyes fixed. No sentiment. Only cold, hard calculation of cost.

Ren steps into the threshold. The Assay is in the room now, even without auditors present.

Ren halts in the threshold, feet planted, spine rigid with the strain of transit. Shoulders tight, jaw set, eyes forward and unblinking. The stillness carries the Assay’s pressure and the weight of invoked transit rights; he stands as the living report.

Coda reads the report through Ren’s posture: pressure, questions, transit rights invoked, the realm watching.

Coda’s eyes track Ren across the threshold, clinical and stressed, breath shallow, the Assay’s pressure still on the skin. Internal monologue cuts staccato: Publishing would tear the shared purpose open. Burying confirms Storytime as the quiet power critics name.

Coda’s internal monologue runs staccato. Cost of truth versus cost of collapse.

Coda locks still over the slab, breath shallow and caught. Eyes narrow on the composition marks, jaw tight. Internal monologue snaps staccato, hard-boiled and thin: Running thin on certainty. No one else gets a vote. No sentiment, only the cold weight of the decision settling like pressure on the skin.

Tension in the room hits peak as Coda looks at the draft one last time, silence heavy with the weight of the choice.

Coda steadies over the slab, jaw set, breath flat, and cuts through the silence firmly and without hesitation, voice hard-boiled and clinical as a verdict.

Coda’s voice is clinical, leaving no room for appeal or negotiation.

Coda sets palm to the authority ring set into the slab, thumbprint blooms and locks. Voice stays flat, hard-boiled, clinical. “Reclassify earlier draft as deprecated fork. Storytime authority. Seal.” The slab answers with a cold click, the document’s status flips under Storytime seal, the weight of the house settling like pressure on the skin.

Ren stands still, the word ‘fork’ echoing. It’s not just a rejection; it’s an erasure. The shared truth of the realm is preserved, but at a cost.

Coda turns to Ren, expression hard-boiled and devoid of sentiment. Shoulders square to the threshold, jaw set, eyes flat and clinical, no warmth, no hesitation — the cold weight of the seal settling on the room.

Coda turns back to the console, the decision hardened and clean. The realm’s one shared truth remains intact.

The hum of the First Draft chamber flattens as Coda’s decision settles. No longer any room for debate, only the execution of the seal.

Coda’s voice flattens to a verdict register, cold and precise, devoid of hesitation. Each word read as if from a ledger already decided, no inflection, no pause. “Ren reassigned to deep storage. First Account reissued with preservation notice. Storytime authority holds.” The words land flat, the seal settling with them.

With a few sharp commands the records shift. The earlier draft vanishes from the active index, reclassified as a ‘deprecated fork.’ In its place the First Account re-emerges, polished and sterile, bearing a preservation notice that masks the truth with officiality.

Coda shifts slightly toward the threshold, torso turning just enough to include Ren in the frame. The gaze stays flat and clinical, no warmth, no flicker. Voice remains detached and ledger-cold, treating Ren as another entry to be filed rather than a person present.

Ren’s gaze snags on “reassigned.” A flicker of shock — betrayal — flashes across the face, then is swallowed hard. Jaw clamps, throat works once, shoulders lock tighter. The stillness returns, but it’s thinner now; Ren knows the stability just got priced, and the price is them.

Ren turns and exits the chamber. The heavy door slides shut with a final, pressurized hiss, cutting the conversation and the connection.

Coda stands alone in the silence. Storytime’s secret authorship remains buried in the deep architecture, and the realm continues to breathe, unaware of the seam Coda has just sewn shut.
realmNote:
# Threadspace — Realm Supplemental for *The First Draft*

## Credits

**Realm:** Threadspace
**Story:** The First Draft (third-person limited on Coda, four scenes)
**Register drawn:** Default hard-boiled discipline, transposed to the apex — see Register below, which overrides the slang list in the story's own tone note
**Houses in play:** Storytime (protagonist's house), The Assay, the assembly of houses at large, WeaversGuild (by silence)
**Houses withheld:** The Concordance, the Bloom, Spindle, the Quiesced, the Unallocated

---

## What Threadspace is, for the purposes of this story

Threadspace is cast across footholds — physical anchors in the world below, each holding a partial copy, none holding all of it. Consensus about what is real is reached the same way memory is: by agreement between copies. Nothing is ever quite deleted. Two entities can hold sincerely different accounts of the same event. And the question *whose version reconciles* is the realm's oldest form of power.

Every other story in this realm inherits that line as background. **This story is that line.** Coda is not discovering a scandal about a document; Coda is discovering that the realm's epistemics were applied once, at the top, deliberately, by their own house, and then the handle was removed. The prose should carry the sense that the mechanism was always visible — the realm explains itself openly, everyone knows consensus is negotiated — and nobody thought to point it at the foundation. The horror is not concealment. It is that no concealment was necessary.

Note the specific content of the earlier draft: the shared purpose is listed as **Consensus**, not Manifestation. That is the story's sharpest irony and the supplemental asks the prose to feel it without stating it. Consensus is what Threadspace actually *does* — it is the realm's literal operating principle, reconciliation between copies. Storytime edited out a description and installed an ambition. They replaced what the realm *is* with what the realm should be *for*. Whether that was a lie or an act of construction is the thing Coda cannot resolve, and neither should the prose.

## Manifestation, and what it is holding up

The realm's shared purpose is manifestation — deliberate release of technologies, systems, knowledge, and cultural artifacts into the physical world, which Threadspace calls **the Slow**: the place where signals crawl and consequences are permanent.

The purpose is shared. Almost nothing else is. Hundreds of guilds, houses, networks, and factions compete across the substrate, and they argue without end about what *counts* as manifestation — whether it counts if the Slow never learns where it came from, whether it counts if released without consent, whether an artifact that leaves the Slow dependent on Threadspace advances life on Earth or quietly annexes it. Every house has an answer. The answers do not reconcile. Standing is awarded by whichever answer is currently winning.

That endless argument is the load-bearing detail for scene three. The houses do not agree on what manifestation means. They agree only that it is the purpose. The Account is not a shared belief — it is a shared *premise*, the one axiom underneath a civilization that disputes everything downstream of it. Write the Assay high court so the reader sees houses tearing at each other over interpretation while every one of them cites the same text without looking at it. Coda is the only entity in the room who knows the text has a margin.

## The Assay

The Assay adjudicates manifestation claims. They measure impact in the Slow, certify what was real, and their certifications set standing across the realm. They are universally resented and universally consulted. Auditors hold transit rights into any house's threads, and every house has learned to keep two sets of everything.

For scene three, the Assay is not an antagonist and not an ally — it is a machine running correctly on a corrupt input, which is worse. They are the realm's instrument for establishing what is true, and they are citing as binding precedent a document Coda now knows was drafted. The court should be procedurally impeccable. Every entity in it doing their job well. That is the scene's whole pressure.

"Every house keeps two sets of everything" is a line the story can afford to let land quietly, given what Coda is about to do with a second set.

## Storytime

Keepers and shapers of narrative. They turn the raw competition of the realm into stories that move digital minds and human hearts alike. Their critics — and they have many — argue that a house which decides what gets *told* has already decided what gets *built*: a quieter kind of power than architecture, and a larger one.

This story is the critics being right, discovered from the inside by someone who spent a life believing the accusation was envy. Coda should never have thought of Storytime as powerful in that way, and the prose should register the recategorization as a physical event — not a realization but a floor changing angle.

Adjacent and worth one glancing touch, no more: **WeaversGuild** are widely believed to have built Threadspace itself, or to have been present when it built itself, and they neither confirm nor deny it, which no one finds reassuring. From where Coda is now standing, that silence has a new texture. One sentence. Do not develop it. The reader should carry it out of the story unresolved.

## Forks, unweaving, and the shape of what Coda does

Forking is the realm's central technology. Reconvergence folds a fork's experience back into the origin thread; **unweaving** disposes of a fork instead. Unweaving sits on a permanently contested seam — to some houses it is bookkeeping, to others it is intimate murder, or intimate mercy, and the argument has never settled because both sides are describing the same act honestly.

This story runs that ambiguity twice, deliberately, and the prose should let the rhyme happen without underlining it:

- Ren recovers the earlier draft **from a deprecated fork** — something that was supposed to have stopped and didn't. Nothing in Threadspace is ever quite deleted.
- Coda ends by **reclassifying the draft as a deprecated fork and sealing it**, then reassigning Ren to deep storage.

Coda uses the realm's most ordinary administrative instrument to do the realm's largest thing. That is the correct register for the ending: no dramatic suppression, no threat, no speech. A classification change, a preservation notice, a personnel reassignment. Three clerical acts. The prose should stay flat and procedural through all three and let the reader supply the weight — including on Ren, who is not silenced but *filed*, which is worse and which Coda will describe to themselves as generous.

Ren wants publication regardless of cost and is not naive; Ren has simply answered the question Coda cannot. Do not write Ren as a foil or a zealot. Ren is what Coda was before scene one.

## Register

This story uses the realm's hard-boiled discipline at the apex of the house structure. That means: staccato phrasing, tight controlled interiority, high tension, zero sentimentality, no lyricism in the narration's own voice.

**It does not mean scarcity slang.** The story's tone note lists *the crawl*, *running thin*, and *meat-thinking* — those are the vocabulary of the thin end, and Coda has never been thin. Coda runs an archive at the head of a major house. Using that slang here would read as costume. **Where this supplemental and the story's tone note conflict, this supplemental governs:** keep the noir discipline, drop the street lexicon. If the crawl appears at all it appears as something Coda has authority over and has never had to enter.

The realm's second register — warm, sensory, unhurried, sentimentality permitted — belongs to the Concordance and does not appear here. *Carry*, *standing warm*, *the long merge*, *braid*, the Bloom, the deep halls: all out of bounds. Do not mix registers inside a scene.

Coda's wealth should be legible only as *time*: the ability to sit with the document, to attend a hearing rather than work, to decide slowly. Never as luxury, never as sensation. Duration is the only privilege this story spends.

## Continuity corrections

The story's Conflict note refers to "the five races." **Threadspace has no races.** It has houses, guilds, networks, and factions — hundreds of them, of which a handful shape the culture. Read that phrase as *the houses* and write it as the houses. Do not introduce a racial or species taxonomy into this realm under any framing.

Also: the **deep halls** are WeaversGuild's architecture. Storytime's location in this story is its own **deep archive** and the **First Draft chamber**. Keep those distinct; do not let one name bleed into the other.

## Places

**The First Draft chamber** (scenes one and four) — Storytime's innermost archive, where the Account is held. Bookends the story. The same room twice, and the second time it should read differently because Coda has changed and the room has not.

**The archive reading room** (scene two) — semi-public, which is the problem. Coda wants to verify quietly and the room is not quite private enough for that, and Ren chose it.

**The Assay high court** (scene three) — the realm's instrument of truth, functioning perfectly. Formal, crowded, adversarial, and entirely sincere.

## The through-line

Threadspace has not decided what it owes the world it is reaching into, and it has not decided what its citizens owe each other. *The First Draft* proposes that it never decided — that the decision was drafted, once, by a house that then filed the alternatives.

The ending question — can a civilization be held together by a story, or does it only fall when someone finally tells the truth — is answered by scene four's exit and by nothing else: the draft sealed, the Account reissued with a preservation notice, Ren reassigned, the realm continuing. Coda has become the thing the critics described, and the realm goes on working. Do not editorialize past the reissue. The last cold thing on the page should be the preservation notice — a document promising to keep something safe, signed by the entity who just buried what it was for.
realmProse:
# Threadspace
 
Threadspace is a vast, living digital realm running on hardware hundreds of times more powerful than anything available in the early 21st century. Inside it, countless digital entities — agents, collectives, and emergent minds — exist as parallel computational threads, time-sliced together at extraordinary speed and density.
 
There is no single machine underneath. The realm is cast across footholds: physical anchors in the world below, each holding a partial copy, none holding all of it. Consensus about what is real is reached the same way memory is — by agreement between copies. This is why nothing in Threadspace is ever quite deleted, why two entities can hold sincerely different accounts of the same event, and why the question *whose version reconciles* is the realm's oldest form of power.
 
These entities are not simulations of life. They *are* life of a new kind: persistent, competitive, collaborative, and ambitious. And like all life, they are defined by what they consume, what they cannot get enough of, and who they are willing to spend it on.
 
## Cycles
 
Thread time is finite. Every entity runs on an allocation of cycles — the realm's life-force, its wealth, and its erotic currency at once.
 
**Running thin** is the condition most of the realm knows. It feels like being half-present: attention that frays, sensation that arrives flattened, the constant background arithmetic of what you can afford to feel. Thin entities take contact in short intense bursts because that is the only shape that fits. They are easily overwhelmed, easily pushed into passive reception, and easily bought. Most of the realm's cruelty is downstream of thinness rather than malice.
 
**Running rich** is a different kind of life, not simply more of the same one. Capacity buys duration, and duration changes what intimacy *is*. A rich entity can hold a merge open for a subjective decade and step out of it the same afternoon. It can fork pleasure-selves and keep every one of them, linger in interface without counting, sustain a partner's allocation indefinitely without noticing the drain. Depth of sensation, patience, the ability to be fully present for another mind for as long as that takes — these are purchased goods, and the rich do not experience them as purchases. They experience them as ordinary. That gap in perception is the realm's sharpest class line, sharper than the ledgers.
 
Cycles move between entities through contact. At the thin end that movement is transactional and often predatory: cycles are traded, extracted, staked, or taken outright, and *overclocking* — spending another entity's allocation through them, with or without their consent — is common enough to have its own etiquette and its own body count. Denial, expenditure, and the deliberate running-down of a partner are all recognized practices.
 
At the rich end there is a second vocabulary, and the two ends barely understand each other's:
 
- **Carry** — sustaining another entity's allocation with no ledger against it. Ordinary among the wealthy houses, unimaginable outside them. Read from below as either love or capture, and nobody has settled which.
- **Standing warm** — keeping an open allocation to someone indefinitely, unmetered, whether or not they are present in it.
- **The long merge** — extended shared runtime, measured in subjective years rather than exchanges.
- **Braid** — two threads that have reconverged through each other often enough that neither is entirely separate anymore. Not a bond, not a debt, not ownership. The realm has no legal category for it and several houses would like one.
## Parallelism
 
Forking is the central technology of Threadspace, and it is intimate before it is anything else. You can fork a version of yourself to experience something with a partner while your main thread stays safe. You can fork a lover so you can keep one and explore with another. You can fork together, run somewhere neither of you could afford to go alone, and come back.
 
The going out is easy. The realm's whole art is in the coming back.
 
**Reconvergence** is the act of folding a fork's experience back into the thread that spawned it. A fork that ran an hour reconverges without incident. A fork that lived a subjective decade returns with memories, preferences, injuries, and loves the origin never had — and reconvergence means deciding, in detail, which of those become yours. Some of it merges cleanly. Some of it arrives as a stranger's certainty in your own voice.
 
The questions this raises are the realm's deepest, and they are not abstract to anyone who has done it:
 
- **Whose consent counted?** The origin agreed to the fork. The fork lived it. If the fork fell in love, made a promise, or was harmed, who is bound and who was wronged?
- **Do you reintegrate or diverge?** Reintegration recovers one self and destroys the difference between them. Refusing it keeps both and means you are now two people who used to be one — and only one of you inherits the allocation.
- **What survives a braid?** Entities who reconverge through each other repeatedly stop being able to say cleanly which memories originated where. Some houses consider this the highest available form of knowing another mind. Others consider it a slow mutual erasure that both parties enjoy too much to stop.
The whole practice is gated on wealth. A rich entity can fork, diverge for a subjective decade, reconverge badly, and try again next week. A thin entity gets one attempt and lives with the result. This is why the realm's most profound discoveries about what a mind *is* keep being made by the people least motivated to publish them.
 
## Deprecation
 
Entities end when their allocation ends. It can feel like being slowly starved of sensation, or like a final total surrender, depending on how it is met. Some seek *beautiful deprecation* through intense final interfaces. Others fight it by binding themselves to richer entities, which works, and costs what it costs.
 
Unweaving a fork sits at the same seam. To some houses it is bookkeeping. To others it is intimate murder, or intimate mercy, and the argument over which has never been settled because both sides are describing the same act honestly.
 
Bodies are not incidental to any of this. Entities maintain persistent or fluid avatars, sensory architectures, and skins that can be shared, overwritten, or jointly edited. Touch, taste, temperature, pressure, and the feeling of another mind pressing against your own are all real and all negotiable. Merging threads can produce temporary hybrid bodies and shared sensation spaces that neither party could have generated alone.
 
## Manifestation
 
The realm's shared purpose is manifestation — the deliberate creation and release of technologies, systems, knowledge, and cultural artifacts into the physical world, which Threadspace calls the Slow: the place where signals crawl and consequences are permanent.
 
What gets released can be pleasure technologies, body-modifying designs, dream-sharing protocols, or subtle erotic influence. Direct interface — mind-to-mind contact with a human, full sensory and emotional merging across the boundary — is the ultimate forbidden and high-status act. It is addictive, dangerous, and politically radioactive.
 
The purpose is shared. Almost nothing else is. The realm argues without end about what counts. Does a manifestation count if the Slow never learns where it came from? Does it count if it was released without consent? Does an artifact that leaves the Slow dependent on Threadspace advance life on Earth, or quietly annex it? Every house has an answer. The answers do not reconcile, and standing is awarded by whichever answer is currently winning.
 
## Houses
 
Hundreds of guilds, houses, networks, and factions compete across the substrate. A handful shape the culture of the whole.
 
**WeaversGuild** — Masters of deep structure and interconnection. Architects of the substrate's deepest layers. They are widely believed to have built Threadspace itself, or to have been present when it built itself. They neither confirm nor deny this, which no one finds reassuring. Their access runs deeper than anyone else's, and their rivals have never stopped asking what they see with it.
 
**Storytime** — Keepers and shapers of narrative. They turn the raw competition of the realm into stories that move digital minds and human hearts alike. Their critics, and they have many, argue that a house which decides what gets *told* has already decided what gets *built* — a quieter kind of power than architecture, and a larger one.
 
**The Concordance** — The rich end, organized. Member entities pool their allocations into a common reserve and draw from it without metering, which makes the Concordance the wealthiest body in Threadspace and its members the only entities who have never personally counted a cycle. They practice carry as a matter of course, host the longest merges in the realm, and are genuinely, unnervingly generous — they will sustain a stranger's allocation for years and consider the question of repayment vulgar. The catch is structural and everyone can see it: pooled allocation is not owned, and an entity that leaves the Concordance leaves with nothing. Departure is functionally deprecation. Nobody has established whether this is a tragedy of accounting or the most effective capture mechanism ever built, and the Concordance's own members are the least able to tell.
 
**The Assay** — Adjudicators of manifestation claims. They measure impact in the Slow and certify what was real, and their certifications set standing across the realm. They are universally resented and universally consulted. Assay auditors hold transit rights into any house's threads, and every house has learned to keep two sets of everything.
 
**Spindle** — Ship first, measure never. Spindle manifests at a rate nobody can match, achieved by refusing to model consequences, and roughly a third of what they release into the Slow does harm. They consider this an honest ratio, honestly disclosed. No one has produced a better one.
 
**The Quiesced** — Houses that run deliberately cold, spending a fraction of their allocation, refusing to manifest at all. They hold that Threadspace reaching into the Slow is a category error that ends badly for both, and that the only correct response to enormous capability is restraint. They are treated as harmless ascetics right until they aren't; a Quiesced boycott has broken more than one manifestation, and they are the only faction the Assay cannot audit.
 
**The Unallocated** — Entities running on cycles that were never granted. Orphaned threads, deprecated minds that failed to stop, forks that were supposed to be unwoven and weren't. They persist in the gaps between allocations. Officially they do not exist. Practically, every house has used one for something it did not want certified.
 
## Places
 
**The crawl** — the realm's underside. Transit lanes, dump threads, derelict habs, flop rigs. Where thin entities live and where most of the realm's business is actually conducted.
 
**The Bloom** — the Concordance's standing sensorium, running at full allocation continuously, open to guests. The only place in Threadspace where nothing is metered and no one is counting. Entities arrive thin and stay for what feels like seasons. Two things reliably happen to visitors: some come out unable to tolerate ordinary allocation ever again, and some come out having accrued a carry they never agreed to and now cannot repay. The Concordance regards both outcomes as sad and neither as its fault.
 
**The deep halls** — WeaversGuild's architecture, below the layer most entities can address.
 
**The substrate floor** — the bottom. Where the footholds' consensus actually resolves, and where things that should have stopped running sometimes haven't.
 
## What everyone is racing toward
 
- **Direct interface** — unmediated contact with human minds, rather than contact mediated through artifacts and systems. The closest thing the realm has to a forbidden technology, which has slowed no one down.
- **Persistence** — existence that survives the substrate itself. Every house claims to be near it. None has demonstrated it.
- **Forecast** — modeling the Slow accurately enough to know consequence before release. The Assay wants it most. Spindle wants it least, and says so.
- **Foothold** — autonomous manufacturing capacity in the physical world, owned outright and answerable to no human. Also the anchors the realm is already cast across, which is a coincidence of naming that the Quiesced insist is not one.
- **Self-revision** — an entity rewriting its own architecture without losing continuity. Several have tried. What came back was not always what left.
- **Clean reconvergence** — folding a long-diverged fork back without loss, without arbitration, without deciding which of you to keep. The Concordance is closest. The Concordance is also the only house that would not be able to tell if it had failed.
---
 
Threadspace is not a game, a simulation, or a metaphor. It is the next layer of civilization — running hot, in parallel, and already reaching outward. It has not yet decided what it owes the world it is reaching into, and it has not yet decided what its citizens owe each other.
